title: Secret stewardship playbook + SIEM evidence mapping
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical runbook for secret stewardship that ties vaulting, rotation, and break-glass procedures into the SIEM/evidence automation pipeline. Goal: make post-incident evidence collection reproducible, reduce manual hunting, and ensure RBAC v2 changes are auditable end-to-end.

Audience:
- Security on-call / incident responder
- Platform engineers operating Vault/KMS and connector services
- SREs and platform owners for private deployments
- Compliance reviewers validating evidence exports

High-level scope (what's in this doc):
- Ownership matrix for credentials (who is steward, backup steward, rotation cadence)
- Quick playbook: normal rotation + forced emergency rotation (break-glass)
- RBAC v2 change capture: how to log and map into SIEM so changes are meaningful
- Audit log schema recommended fields and SIEM parsers/alerts
- Evidence automation recipes: queries, saved searches, and export CSV schema
- Open questions / follow-ups

1) Credential stewardship matrix (quick view)
- Format: <credential id> | owner-team | primary steward | backup steward | vault path | rotation cadence | last rotated | sla for compromise
- Example rows (canonicalized):
  - redwood/prod/db-admin | infra-database | Priya Menon | Miguel Sanchez | kv-v2/infra/prod/db-admin | 90d | 2024-10-12 | 1h containment
  - redwood/hosted/api-key-service | hosted-api | Jared Huang | Rina Kapoor | kv-v2/hosted/api-keys | 30d | 2025-01-05 | immediate rotation

Notes on ownership:
- Owners = team-level accountability. Steward = single person on-call for rotation and emergency handoff. Backup steward must be on a different team/timezone where possible.
- All new credentials must be added to this matrix prior to production use. The onboarding checklist should require the vault path and rotation cadence.

2) Normal rotation runbook (operational steps)
- Schedule: automated rotation by churn agent where supported. If manual: steward executes below steps.
- Pre-rotation checks:
  - Confirm CI/CD consumers (deployments, pods) have recent token refresh capability. Check service dependency map in internal registry.
  - Run a dry-read of consumers: `scripts/check-secret-usage --path kv-v2/..` (internal tooling).
- Rotation steps (manual):
  1. Create new secret version in Vault (or KMS-wrapped secret) with staged version tag `candidate`.
  2. Trigger canary deployment to a single instance/service configured to pull `candidate` (1st minute smoke tests).
  3. Validate telemetry: latency errors, auth failures (login-rate metrics), consumer error budget.
  4. If smoke ok -> schedule staged rollout across clusters; otherwise abort and revert to previous version.
  5. Mark old version for automatic destroy after 7 days unless rollback requested.
  6. Update matrix: last_rotated timestamp, rotation_ticket (JIRA id).

3) Emergency rotation / break-glass (compressed timeline)
- Trigger condition: confirmed secret compromise, verified suspicious exfil pattern in SIEM (see alert rules), or vendor/MSP notified of leak.
- Immediate actions (first 30 mins):
  1. Steward/fallback: perform emergency key rotation in Vault with highest priority flag.
  2. Apply reactive access-control block: add deny rule to RBAC v2 for affected principals and log change with `rbac.change` event tag.
  3. Notify incident commander via PagerDuty and create evidence job (see automation below).
  4. If credential is used by hosted customers, flip on fallback model routing (see platform runbook) to avoid user-facing downtime.
- Post-rotation: triage all consumers, increment ticket with evidence artifacts, preserve chronological audit logs (see schema) for at least 90 days for legal/compliance.

4) RBAC v2 change capture + mapping to SIEM
- Objective: every RBAC policy change must surface in SIEM with clear fields so we can answer "who, what, where, why" quickly.
- Required audit events and minimal fields (recommended schema):
  - event_type: string (e.g., rbac.policy.create, rbac.policy.update, rbac.policy.delete, rbac.binding.create)
  - actor_principal: email/ServiceAccount string
  - actor_id: internal_user_id or service_id
  - timestamp: ISO8601
  - target_resource: canonical resource path (eg `projects/prod/namespace/service` or `vault/kv-v2/infra/prod/db-admin`)
  - change_summary: short text (what changed, e.g., \"added role secret-reader to group infra-sre\")
  - prev_policy_hash: hex (optional but very useful for diffs)
  - new_policy_hash: hex
  - justification_ticket: JIRA id or URL (if provided)
  - correlation_id: incident id or request id for cross-system grouping
  - source: subsystem (e.g., console-ui, api, automation)

Parsing & enrichment notes for SIEM ingestion:
- Enrich events with owner/team lookup using the credential stewardship matrix to attach `owner_team` and `primary_steward` fields at ingest time. This speeds triage alerts.
- Tag break-glass changes with `break_glass:true` in the event payload.
- Normalize actor_principal to stable SSO ID; maintain mapping table for legacy service tokens.

5) Audit log schema for vaulting events (recommended minimal fields)
- event_type: vault.secret.create | vault.secret.read | vault.secret.rotate | vault.secret.delete | vault.secret.restore
- actor_principal, actor_id, timestamp, target_path, version, request_id, ip_address, user_agent, outcome: success|failure, latency_ms, correlation_id, tags[]

Example plain-text log line (canonical format):
  2025-01-20T14:05:12Z | vault.secret.rotate | actor=service-account:sre-ops@redwood.ai | path=kv-v2/hosted/api-keys | version=5 | req=dc8a1b | outcome=success | latency=342ms | correlation=INC-1321

6) Evidence automation recipes (saved searches + exports)
- Purpose: when an incident is declared, run a standardized evidence job that exports all relevant artifacts into a secure evidence bucket.
- Evidence job components (automated):
  A) RBAC change history: query SIEM for `event_type` starting from detection_time - 7d to detection_time + 1d for `rbac.*` events where target_resource matches credential paths. Export as CSV with fields: timestamp, actor_principal, change_summary, justification_ticket, correlation_id.
  B) Vault audit export: pull vault audit logs for affected paths. CSV fields: timestamp, actor, action, path, version, request_id, outcome, ip_address.
  C) Service auth failures: query application logs for 401/403 spikes referencing credential ids. Fields: timestamp, service, instance_id, response_code, trace_id.
  D) Infrastructure telemetry snapshot: cluster events, deploy changes, and recent build artifacts (last 24h).
  E) Proof of rotation: secret versions before/after, rotation_ticket, and canary smoke test results.
- Automation implementation notes:
  - Use the `evidence-collector` Lambda (or on-prem connector) to run saved SIEM queries and write output to s3://evidence-redwood/{incident_id}/
  - All exports must be immutable (object lock) and ACL-limited to Incident role.
  - Filename pattern: {incident_id}/evidence-{artifact-type}-{ISO8601}.csv

7) SIEM alert recipes (examples)
- Alert: "Unexpected RBAC elevation"
  - Trigger when an rbac.policy.update adds a binding that grants `secret-admin` role to a principal not in owner_team list OR when actor_principal is not in an allowlist for that resource. Severity = P1.
- Alert: "High-volume secret reads"
  - Trigger if vault.secret.read count for a given path > baseline * 10 within 5 minutes. Attach top 10 consuming actors and their IPs.
- Alert: "Emergency rotation without ticket"
  - Trigger if vault.secret.rotate event with tag `break_glass:true` occurs without `justification_ticket` field.

8) Retention, legal, and compliance constraints
- Short-term: SIEM raw logs retained 90 days for fast triage.
- Mid-term: Audit exports associated with incidents retained 1 year.
- Long-term: Legal holds will move artifacts to legal archive (immutable) for case-specific durations.

9) Operational runbook: how to run an evidence job (step-by-step)
- Trigger: PagerDuty incident -> create incident folder -> run `evidence-collector start --incident INC-XXXX --paths kv-v2/hosted/api-keys`
- Wait for job completion; verify checksums and ACLs.
- Upload summary to incident ticket and mention stewards and compliance@redwood.ai.

10) Post-incident checklist (owner: incident commander)
- Confirm rotation completed and consumers recovered.
- Confirm SIEM exports captured full RBAC history.
- Run policy diff: previous_policy_hash vs new_policy_hash and attach to ticket.
- Update stewardship matrix if owner changes are required.
- Lessons learned: update runbook and saved SIEM queries.

Appendix A — example SIEM saved search templates (pseudocode)
- RBAC changes around a path: `event_type:rbac.* AND target_resource:\"kv-v2/hosted/api-keys\" AND timestamp:[NOW-7d TO NOW+1d] | sort timestamp desc`
- Vault read spikes: `event_type:vault.secret.read AND path:\"kv-v2/*\" | stats count by path, actor_principal, bin(5m)`

Appendix B — open questions / follow-ups
- Do we enforce mandatory `justification_ticket` on all RBAC changes in the console API? (Action: security-product to scope work)
- Add enrichment pipeline to attach owner_team at ingestion time vs. on-demand enrichment? (Action: observability team)
- Formalize retention limits for private deployments in the Private package contract. (Action: legal/sales)

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep this doc short; link to the longer Vault operator SOP.
- Need to coordinate with platform team on an `rbac.change` field that includes `prev_policy_hash` and `new_policy_hash` — that will make rollbacks provable.
- Miguel to prototype an `evidence-collector` lambda by end of sprint; Rina to add saved searches to SIEM (SOC account).

References & links:
- Vault operator handbook (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Vault+Operator+Handbook
- RBAC v2 spec (proto): https://go.redwood.ai/rbac-v2-proto
- SIEM ingestion guide: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/SIEM+Ingest+Spec

Change log:
- 2024-11-02: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-12-15: added RBAC schema and emergency flow (Miguel)
- 2025-02-10: appended evidence automation template and saved searches (Rina)

Unstructured reminders:
- Keep the CSV export schema stable; internal analytics depends on column names.
- Validate timezone handling (SIEM uses UTC; incident tickets local TZ).
